title: Gradient of curves and rate of changes
competency: Find the slope of a secant line and link it to the average rate of change.

keywords.def: A line through two points of a curve.
A line that touches a curve at one point and has its steepness there.
The slope of a line: rise ÷ run.

en.text: A secant line passes through two points of a curve. Its slope (y₁ − y₀)/(x₁ − x₀) is the average rate of change of the function between those points. A tangent line touches the curve at one point and shows its steepness there.

am.text: ሴካንት መስመር በኩርባው ሁለት ነጥቦች ያልፋል። ስሎፑ በሁለቱ ነጥቦች መካከል ያለው አማካይ የለውጥ መጠን ነው።

screens.title: Secant and tangent
paras: A secant line passes through two points of a curve.
A tangent line touches the curve at one point, the point of tangency.
Gradient (slope) describes steepness and direction: positive goes up, negative goes down, zero is horizontal.

screens.title: Slope of a secant
paras: For A(x₀, y₀) and B(x₁, y₁): slope = Δy/Δx = (y₁ − y₀)/(x₁ − x₀).
screens.note: Slope of a secant line = average rate of change.

screens.ask: Find the slope of the line through (−3, −5) and (3, 11): ___

screens.title: Put the steps for a secant slope in order
items: Write the two x-values a and b
screens.why:
First fix the interval [a, b].
Then find the two y-values f(a) and f(b).
Subtract them for Δy.
Divide by Δx = b − a to get the slope.
screens.clue: You need the y-values before you can subtract them.

screens.ask: Find the slope of the line through (3, −5) and (−2, 9): ___
screens.why:
Δy = 9 − (−5) = 14.
Δx = −2 − 3 = −5.
Slope = 14/(−5) = −14/5 = −2.8.
Trap: taking 9 − (−5) but 3 − (−2) mixes the order and gives +14/5.
screens.clue: Keep the same order on top and bottom.

test.text: True or false: the slope of a secant line equals the average rate of change.
test.why:
A secant goes through (a, f(a)) and (b, f(b)).
Its slope is (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a).
That is the average rate of change on [a, b]. True.
